Seminar Title:

Constructed Wetland Integrated with Microbial Fuel Cell for Simultaneous Treatment of Chromium Contaminated Wastewater and Bioelectricity Generation

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Divyani Kumari ( Rollno : 520bm3007)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

03 Sep 2026 11 AM

Contact:

Kasturi Dutta

Abstract:

India is the fourth-largest chromite reserves, primarily in Odisha at Sukinda Valley. Despite its economic significance, the region faces severe side effects due to Hexavalent Chromium (Cr(VI)), a toxic heavy metal. Conventional treatment methods such as&nbsp adsorption, membrane filtration, electrochemical processes, and bioremediation show limitations. Constructed wetlands (CWs), displays interplay of adsorption, filtration, microbial action, and phytoremediation, offer a robust alternative. When coupled with a microbial fuel cell (MFC), the system further benefits from strong redox gradients that enhance pollutant removal and generate bioelectricity. This study evaluated a CW-MFC system for Cr (VI) treatment and energy recovery. First, planted (CW-P) and unplanted (CW-UP) wetlands were compared at high Cr (VI) loads (up to 200 mg/L). CW-P showed superior performance, achieving 99.98% Cr(VI) and 84.45% COD removal at an optimal HRT of 48 h, supported by higher microbial abundance dominated by Proteobacteria and Bacteroidia. The system was then integrated with MFCs using cement graphite (CG) and graphite electrodes, where CG-CW-MFC produced higher voltages (465.6 and 191.45 mV). A reductive substrate of nano-ZVI water hyacinth biochar further enhanced performance, with maximum voltage output of 436.52 mV and dominant microbial presence in the cathodic layer. Finally, single-anode (SA-CW-MFC) and multi-anode configurations were tested for simulated chromite wastewater, with SA-CW-MFC showing better voltage output (506 mV). Lastly, SA-CW-MFC was co-treatment with kitchen and raw chromite mine wastewater achieved 96.83% Cr (VI). Life-cycle and techno-economic assessments affirmed the environmental and economic viability of the technology, establishing CW-MFC as a promising next-generation sustainable treatment solution.
